sources.source_name: Federal Reserve FEDS2007-13: Mark Carlson historical study of1987 crash
sources.notes: Archived abstract explicitly dated Last update: May1 2007 (https://www.federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/2007/200713/200713abs.html); this is an archive revision date, not the original paper date (November2006) or event date. Retrospective Federal Reserve research distinguishes October19 crash and October20 visible liquidity support. It does not establish precise causal weights for scenario returns.

Official announcement identifies July 1990 peak retrospectively. March 1991 trough was not announced until December 22 1992, after scenario endpoint; not presented as a contemporaneously known January 1992 fact.

sources.source_name: Apple investor FAQ: historical stock splits
sources.notes: Issuer table dates two-for-one split June 16, 1987; later splits uniformly rescale the earlier prices. No extra split return is added. Current retrospective archive; original publication date and hosting revision date are unknown. Retrieved date is not historical publication.

sources.source_name: Apple historical dividend and split table
sources.notes: Original amounts are not split adjusted. April 22 1987 declaration: record May 15, payable June 15, $0.06; July 29 declaration: record Aug 14, payable Sept 15, $0.06. Vendor ex-dates May 11 and Aug 10 fall within Aug 1987 horizon, though second payment follows endpoint. Current backward-adjusted vendor amounts differ by later splits; not separately added. Current retrospective archive; original publication date and hosting revision date are unknown. Retrieved date is not historical publication.

Issuer table puts adjacent splits in 1979 and 1997; none during either selected 1982–87 or 1987–92 holding window. Current reconstruction also reflects later Kyndryl separation; no successor mapping applied within these windows. Current retrospective archive; original publication date and hosting revision date are unknown. Retrieved date is not historical publication.

sources.source_name: GE Aerospace shareholder services and FAQ
sources.notes: Current legal issuer continues historical General Electric lineage; page documents 2021 reverse split and 2023/2024 separations outside Jan 1992 horizon. May 26 1987 two-for-one is recorded in pinned Yahoo events; not independently corroborated by an accessible original GE split announcement. Acquisitions of operating businesses do not themselves require exchanging GE shareholder holdings. Vendor reconstruction reliability remains a limitation. Current retrospective archive; original publication date and hosting revision date are unknown. Retrieved date is not historical publication.
Undated retrospective company history: early PC sales, competition from clones, 1987 PS/2 launch, and the subsequent competitive response. Only facts inside each scenario window are used.

sources.source_name: UPI: IBM reports fourth-quarter loss, will keep cutting jobs
sources.notes: Indexed original archive report consulted. The $2.8 billion annual loss included retiree-benefit accounting and restructuring charges; the copy does not describe it as an operating loss.

sources.source_name: UPI: GE earnings up, stock down sharply
sources.notes: Indexed original archive report consulted: quarterly profit $1.026 billion versus $945 million; financial services, aircraft engines, power systems and appliances helped, while NBC and materials weakened.

sources.source_name: TIME: Apple expands its business-computer market
sources.notes: Contemporary report: Macintosh SE and Macintosh II expanded the business market; second fiscal quarter revenue was $637 million, up 42%. The copy does not use later full-year results for earlier endpoints.

sources.source_name: UPI: Apple Computer reports record quarterly profits
sources.notes: Indexed original archive report consulted: first fiscal quarter net income $121.4 million, up 108%, following the expanded Macintosh line.
Indexed original archive report consulted: 400 layoffs and reserves for restructuring and severance.
